label: Mobile app (iOS / Android)
summary: Native-feeling phone app, one or both operating systems

options.question: Which device frames should be designed?
Which screens to design? (leave as default to take them from the brief)

preview_screen: The home screen inside the first chosen device frame, with status bar, primary content and navigation.
code_target: A responsive prototype in the project's stack (plain HTML, CSS and JS by default) inside device frames (status bar, safe areas, home indicator) with tab or stack navigation and touch interactions. A prototype, not native code.
required_screens: Permission request (if the product uses camera, location, notifications)
required_states: Keyboard open on every screen with an input
Empty, loading skeleton and error for every data screen
Bottom sheet open with its dismiss action
design_guidance: Draw the real device frame: status bar, notch or Dynamic Island, home indicator. Keep content out of the safe areas; extend bar backgrounds into them.
Targets 44x44 (iOS) or 48x48 (Android) at least; primary actions in the lower half.
With 'both' selected, follow each platform's navigation and control conventions, and call out where the two designs differ.
Tappable elements show a pressed state; do not rely on hover.

checks: No content sits under the status bar, notch or home indicator; fixed bars extend into the safe area.
Every interactive target measures at least 44x44 (iOS) or 48x48 (Android), and no two hit areas overlap.
Every screen with an input has a keyboard-open state in which the focused field and its submit action stay visible.
Primary actions are within the lower half of the screen; destructive actions are not next to the easiest reach.
Every gesture (swipe, pull, drag) has a visible tappable alternative.
Every chosen device frame is designed, including the smallest, with no clipped content on it.
Every tappable element has a pressed state; no information depends on hover.
